items.headline: Tech sell-off deepens as investors question AI data-center spending
items.summary: Technology stocks fell sharply, with Nvidia among the largest drags on the S&P 500. The report linked pressure on chipmakers and other AI-infrastructure beneficiaries to concerns that high interest rates could slow data-center expansion.

items.headline: Midterm elections, earnings and jobs data loom for an AI-wary market
items.summary: Reuters reported that Alphabet’s cash burn and disappointing revenue intensified investor concerns about financing the AI-investment theme. Apple, AMD and Palantir were identified as major companies due to report the following week.

items.headline: Nasdaq faces a potential $2 trillion October wipeout as AI spending fears deepen
items.summary: Reuters reported that the Nasdaq 100 had fallen more than 5.8% during October as investors questioned whether expanding AI infrastructure spending would generate returns quickly enough. Meta’s planned $97.5 billion fund raise added to concerns about dilution and financing needs.

items.headline: Amazon and Intel results intensify concerns over Big Tech AI spending
items.summary: Amazon’s Bedrock token volume reportedly grew nearly 17-fold year over year, while Fortune 500 customer spending increased nearly sevenfold. The same report highlighted custom silicon as a possible route to more efficient AI capital expenditure.

items.headline: Global markets react to a fresh AI-euphoria reversal
items.summary: Reuters reported that investors were becoming nervous about hyperscalers’ enormous AI spending plans, including the potential borrowing required to finance the build-out. The report described the market move as a cooling of AI enthusiasm after recent earnings and spending updates.
